did_you_know.text: Did you know? Josiah became king when he was only eight years old, and he reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.
Did you know? In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, Josiah began to seek the God of David; and in the twelfth year he began purifying Judah and Jerusalem by removing idolatry.

Did you know? The purification of the land included smashing the altars of Baal, cutting down the incense altars, and breaking the Asherah poles, idols, and images; he scattered the fragments of the idols over the graves of those who had worshiped them.

Did you know? Josiah’s campaign of purification was not limited to Judah and Jerusalem; it also reached the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, throughout the entire land of Israel.
Did you know? In the eighteenth year of his reign, Josiah worked both to purify the land and to strengthen the Temple, sending officials to organize the restoration work.

Did you know? The Levites performed a variety of duties in the Temple: some supervised the work, while others served as scribes, officials, gatekeepers, and musicians skilled in playing musical instruments.
Did you know? While the money was being removed from the Temple of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law of the Lord, given through Moses, and handed it to Shaphan the secretary.
Did you know? When Josiah heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes—a gesture expressing his shock and submission before the word of the Lord.
Did you know? The delegation sent by Josiah went to Huldah the prophetess, who lived in Jerusalem; after they presented the words of the book to her, she delivered the word of the Lord.
Did you know? Huldah explained that the mercy shown to Josiah was because his heart was tender, he humbled himself before God, tore his clothes, and wept before the Lord.
Did you know? After hearing Huldah’s response, Josiah gathered the elders of Judah and Jerusalem and all the people—from the greatest to the least—in the Temple of the Lord.

Did you know? Josiah made a covenant before the Lord to follow Him and keep His commands, statutes, and laws with all his heart and soul, in accordance with the words of the covenant written in the book.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it is said that Josiah removed all the abominations from every land belonging to the Israelites, and throughout his lifetime the people did not turn away from the Lord, the God of their ancestors.
